planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in early spring in full sun to part shade on well-drained soil; apple rose forms a large, arching shrub, so give it plenty of room from the start.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade on well-drained soil; apple rose is a grey-green-leaved species rose bearing single soft-pink flowers in late spring followed by unusually large, bristly, apple-scented red hips in late summer and fall. The hips are prized across Scandinavia for syrup and jam (classic in Swedish nyponsoppa, rosehip soup), and the bristly texture and size distinguish them from the smaller, smoother hips of Rosa rugosa. The arching shrub needs little care once established beyond an occasional thinning of old canes, and tolerates poor soil and cold winters well.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade; Scarlet Ovation's naturally dwarf habit suits it to tighter spaces than the species.

directions: Plant in part to full shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Scarlet Ovation is a naturally dwarf evergreen huckleberry selection growing only 2-3 feet tall, with bronze-red new spring growth maturing to glossy dark green. Like the species it tolerates deep shade under conifers and bears small, dark-purple, sweet-tart berries used in Pacific Northwest jams and baking. Its compact size makes it a good choice for shaded foundation plantings or a woodland-garden edge where the full-size species would outgrow the space.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade; Inverness forms a denser, more compact hedge than the species.

directions: Plant in part to full shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Inverness is a Marin County selection of evergreen huckleberry chosen for its dense, compact growth habit, making it a reliable choice for a shaded evergreen hedge or screen. It bears the same small, dark-purple, sweet-tart berries as the species, used in Pacific Northwest jams and pies, as a useful bonus on top of its landscape value. Established plants need little supplemental water and tolerate the dry shade found under mature conifers.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Cascade Sunburst tolerates more sun than most evergreen huckleberry selections, which brightens its variegated new growth further.

directions: Plant in full sun to full shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Cascade Sunburst is a Briggs Nursery introduction grown chiefly for its striking coral-pink new growth that matures to green edged in creamy variegation, with the species' typical pale pink urn-shaped spring flowers and edible glossy purple-black berries following in summer. It grows to roughly four feet tall and wide, forming a well-proportioned shrub for a mixed border or foundation planting. Unlike most evergreen huckleberry selections it colors up well in considerable sun, though it still tolerates shade.

planting.note: Plant container stock or suckers in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in part shade; like the species, Golden Ruby suckers readily to form a thicket, so give it room or a root barrier.

directions: Plant in part shade in moist, humus-rich soil; Golden Ruby is a golden-foliaged salmonberry selection that contrasts its bright yellow leaves against deep pink-red spring flowers, brightening a shaded woodland edge well before the fruit appears. It fruits like the species, producing the normal polymorphic salmonberry drupes that range from red to golden-yellow with a juicy, mild flavor, best eaten fresh or in jam. Like all salmonberries it spreads by root suckers to form a thicket over time, so plant it where that spreading habit is wanted or install a barrier to contain it.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Compactum's dwarf size suits foundation plantings and smaller gardens where the full-size species would be too large.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in moist, well-drained soil; Compactum is a dwarf selection of American highbush cranberry reaching only about 5-6 feet tall, roughly half the size of the standard species, while remaining a heavy spring bloomer and fall fruiter. Its white lacecap flower clusters in late spring give way to the same tart red, maple-leaf-shrub drupes used as a traditional cranberry-sauce substitute, held into winter as bird-attracting color. The compact size makes it a practical choice for home gardens and foundation plantings where the full-size species would quickly outgrow the space.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, peaty, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; unlike the typical dioecious species, this self-fertile variety sets fruit from a single plant.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade on acidic, peaty, well-drained soil; hermaphrodite crowberry is a self-fertile botanical variety of crowberry that sets its small black edible berries on a single plant, unlike the typical dioecious species, which needs separate male and female plants to fruit at all. This is a genuinely practical distinction for a home garden where space for only one plant is available. It forms a dwarf, creeping evergreen groundcover similar to the species, tolerating cold, wind, and lean soil, and the berries are traditionally used in Nordic jams and juice.
